core_obligations: Construct the canonical map from the left hand side to the right hand side using functoriality of Tor (proof lines 14993-14997).

Choose a free resolution of the first algebra, base change it and use flatness of the base to identify one intermediate Tor with the base change of Tor over the original ring (proof lines 14999-15010).

Write the outer algebras as filtered colimits of finite free modules by Lazard's theorem and use compatibility of Tor with colimits to show the comparison map is an isomorphism (proof lines 15012-15022).
proof_roadmap: Identify the intermediate Tor by a resolution and flatness (proof lines 14999-15010).
Apply Lazard and colimit compatibility to conclude (proof lines 15012-15023).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the Tor groups of a base changed pair of algebras with the base change of the Tor groups of the original pair, under three flatness hypotheses, and the proof is a 31-line argument in three stages. It first constructs the canonical comparison map from the functoriality of Tor, then computes one of the intermediate Tor groups by a free resolution and uses flatness to identify it with a base change of Tor over the original ring, and finally uses Lazard's theorem to write the outer algebras as filtered colimits of finite free modules so that Tor commutes with the colimit and the identification becomes an isomorphism. Each of the three stages uses exactly one of the hypotheses, and all three are carried out in the source.
